highlights.quote: Absorbed dose \(D\) is the radiation energy absorbed per kilogram of tissue.

Equivalent and effective dose are measured in sievert (Sv); one sievert is large, so everyday values are quoted in millisieverts (mSv).

highlights.quote: Absorbed dose \(D\) is the radiation energy absorbed per kilogram of tissue.
It increases with the strength of the source, the time of exposure and closeness to the source.
Equivalent dose \(H\) weights that absorbed dose for the radiation type: α causes denser ionization than β, γ or X-rays.

Effective dose \(E\) then weights the equivalent dose for the sensitivity of the exposed tissue, so it can represent the overall risk from an exposure: \[ H = D \times W_{\text{radiation}}, \qquad E = H \times W_{\text{tissue}} \] For exposure involving several tissues, add the appropriately weighted contributions to obtain \(E\).
Equivalent and effective dose are measured in sievert (Sv); one sievert is large, so everyday values are quoted in millisieverts (mSv).
